html:
The Battle of Leuctra was fought on 6 July 371 BCE in Boeotia between the Thebans and their allies, led by Epaminondas, and the army of Sparta. Thebes won, and Spartan power in Greece never recovered.

The fight grew out of a quarrel over renewing the King's Peace, which Sparta used to keep Thebes weak. Greek armies usually put their best troops on the right wing. Epaminondas did the opposite: he massed his best men on the left, fifty ranks deep, aimed straight at the Spartan king and his elite on the right, and held back his weaker wing. The Sacred Band, an elite Theban unit under Pelopidas, struck at the key moment. The Spartan line broke, and King Cleombrotus was killed with about four hundred Spartan citizens.

Sparta had very few full citizens, and the loss could not be made good. The myth that Spartans could not be beaten in pitched battle was gone. The next winter Epaminondas invaded the Peloponnese and freed Messenia, founding Messene. His deep, slanting attack was later studied by Philip II of Macedon.
